item.title: Is It Possible for Kids to Control their Emotions? A Child Therapist Weighs In
item.description:
Upon asking if it is possible for kids to control their emotions, it is equally important to ask whether it is reasonable to expect it. As a therapist who has worked with children five years old and older, I will answer yes to both questions. Yes, it is possible for kids to control their emotions. And yes, it is reasonable to expect a child five years old to be able to control their emotions.

However, defining what that control means and looks like is key to understanding how it will look in operation and function in a child. Controlling emotions refers to the ability to identify, steward, and respond to emotional stimulation in a balanced or healthy way versus dismissing or ignoring them. Controlling emotions in therapeutic terms is referred to as emotional regulation.

Emotional regulation is the process of managing the intensity, duration, and expression of emotions to respond correctly to situations while maintaining mental well-being. Note that this definition does not intend for the child to avoid or repress the feelings that arise but requires them to manage their emotional reaction.

Emotional reaction management helps ensure that decision-making does not become overwhelmed and that social interactions remain mostly positive.

Every Child Can Learn About Emotions

Per the National Center for Education Statistics, children can learn more about their emotions than we sometimes give them credit for. Even young children are taking in information, remembering patterns, and beginning to connect what they feel with what is happening around them. By ages 2-3, children can begin holding on to information in meaningful ways.

As they move closer to ages 4-5, their memory, attention, and ability to follow simple steps continue to grow. This matters because emotional regulation is also learned step by step. A child may not always respond perfectly, but with consistent teaching, modeling, and practice, they can learn to pause, name what they feel, and choose a safer or more appropriate response.

Teaching children emotional regulation requires teaching them in a way they can comprehend. Children need the concept of “emotional regulation” broken down into a more understandable construct such as “pause and check in.” Often, taking the foundational meaning of words and using them with a younger mind helps them better connect with meaning.

Emotional regulation at its foundation is all about pausing and checking in with yourself first. Although emotional regulation is profoundly serious, allowing a child to learn emotional regulation by making it into a “tag-your-it” type of game is okay.

As a therapist who has worked with children and adolescents, the intensity can be lessened if fun can be had. However, always remind the child that fun is okay, and safety is the best friend of fun. We can have fun if you are safe, and so is everyone else. This is layered, but it is the step-by-step method that was previously mentioned. Once you convey the concept, begin to build on it to add other important ideas regarding emotional regulation.

What A Child Needs to Know About Their Emotions

The first thing that a child needs to know about their emotions is that they are not bad, stupid, make them an annoying person, make them weird, should make them feel scared, or any other negative conclusion they may have come to.

Children must know that emotions are a part of their human experience and their emotions are God given. The goal is to help them not only regulate their emotions but to understand them so that they can avoid shame or even embarrassment because of what they are feeling.

Here are a few simple phrases that can help children and adolescents feel seen, supported, and less alone in what they are experiencing.

  • “It’s okay to not feel okay.” – Normalizes odd feelings without judgement.
  • “Sadness can feel lonely. Can I sit with you quietly?” – Normalize maintaining connecting during tough times versus isolation.
  • “Crying is okay. I will get you some tissue.” – The focus is getting the child comfortable with being supported while being validated (seen).
  • “Feeling scared is hard. What do you need right now? – The focus is getting the child to speak to how to name what would meet their need, by using their words.

The key is to keep it simple, continue step-by-step and to model. Children need to see that we not only understand but are present. Being present is not just about our bodies being in the same space, meaning proximity. They need to know that an adult is present in their eyes and with their hearts. This matters to any child in any emotional state at any time.

Modeling is one of the most effective ways children learn emotional regulation. Children are always watching how the adults around them respond to frustration, sadness, disappointment, fear, and even joy.

When adults can slow down, name what is happening, and respond steadily, children begin to learn that emotions can be felt without taking over the whole moment. This is not about being perfect in front of a child. It is about allowing the child to see regulation practiced in real time.

One Step Further

The goal is to build a foundation of understanding not only emotional regulation but to also take it one step further to begin establishing good mental health. Think about that for a second, what if it was widespread practice to put into place the building blocks for children to have a good headstart to sound mental health.

Children who understand their emotions grow into adults who understand their emotions as well as how to manage them. Children can control their emotions when they learn that their emotions are a part of their human experience.

As a therapist who is a Christian, I can tell you that unpacking that truth, along with the reality that God equipped us with emotions for a purpose, and that they are good. God speaks of emotions and how to manage them throughout His Word.

A child must know that anger is real and God is aware. Fear is going to show up; God knew it and warned us that we were going to have to stand up to fear, not run from it. With God’s help, they can emotionally regulate.

Children are easy to teach when we know what we are teaching and how to teach it. When controlling emotions is taught with consideration of self, others, environment, and outcome, it helps to create step-by-step instruction, which creates consistency in demonstration and modeling.

As children grow into adolescents the emotional lessons that they learn will undoubtedly stick with them while allowing additional knowledge of more complicated emotional concepts.

Sensitivity can be learned, and due to our culture, which is heavily packed with less-kind television programming, video games, and movie entertainment, sensitivity is an emotion we cannot afford to leave children to gather on their own.

Teaching children how to manage anger and express it in a healthy way is a necessity our current society can no longer ignore. Ignoring emotional health until it becomes a crisis. When a child is in mental crisis, there is less chance of helping them, and it is harder to assist the appointed adult with comprehending what is happening with them in the moment.

The more clarity that can be given to children to help them identify and understand their emotions, the better we can help them manage what they go through while continuing to understand who they are and will become emotionally.

item.description:

Controlling emotions refers to the ability to identify, steward, and respond to emotional stimulation in a balanced or healthy way versus dismissing or ignoring them. Even young children are taking in information, remembering patterns, and beginning to connect what they feel with what is happening around them. The goal is to build a foundation of understanding not only emotional regulation but to also take it one step further to begin establishing good mental health. Think about that for a second, what if it was widespread practice to put into place the building blocks for children to have a good headstart to sound mental health.

Children who understand their emotions grow into adults who understand their emotions as well as how to manage them. Children can control their emotions when they learn that their emotions are a part of their human experience.

As a therapist who is a Christian, I can tell you that unpacking that truth, along with the reality that God equipped us with emotions for a purpose, and that they are good. God speaks of emotions and how to manage them throughout His Word.

A child must know that anger is real and God is aware. Fear is going to show up; God knew it and warned us that we were going to have to stand up to fear, not run from it. With God’s help, they can emotionally regulate.

As children grow into adolescents the emotional lessons that they learn will undoubtedly stick with them while allowing additional knowledge of more complicated emotional concepts.

Sensitivity can be learned, and due to our culture, which is heavily packed with less-kind television programming, video games, and movie entertainment, sensitivity is an emotion we cannot afford to leave children to gather on their own.

Teaching children how to manage anger and express it in a healthy way is a necessity our current society can no longer ignore. Ignoring emotional health until it becomes a crisis. When a child is in mental crisis, there is less chance of helping them, and it is harder to assist the appointed adult with comprehending what is happening with them in the moment.

The more clarity that can be given to children to help them identify and understand their emotions, the better we can help them manage what they go through while continuing to understand who they are and will become emotionally.

Note that this definition does not intend for the child to avoid or repress the feelings that arise but requires them to manage their emotional reaction.

Emotional reaction management helps ensure that decision-making does not become overwhelmed and that social interactions remain mostly positive.

Every Child Can Learn About Emotions

Per the National Center for Education Statistics, children can learn more about their emotions than we sometimes give them credit for. Even young children are taking in information, remembering patterns, and beginning to connect what they feel with what is happening around them. By ages 2-3, children can begin holding on to information in meaningful ways.

As they move closer to ages 4-5, their memory, attention, and ability to follow simple steps continue to grow. This matters because emotional regulation is also learned step by step. A child may not always respond perfectly, but with consistent teaching, modeling, and practice, they can learn to pause, name what they feel, and choose a safer or more appropriate response.

Teaching children emotional regulation requires teaching them in a way they can comprehend. Children need the concept of “emotional regulation” broken down into a more understandable construct such as “pause and check in.” Often, taking the foundational meaning of words and using them with a younger mind helps them better connect with meaning.

Emotional regulation at its foundation is all about pausing and checking in with yourself first. Although emotional regulation is profoundly serious, allowing a child to learn emotional regulation by making it into a “tag-your-it” type of game is okay.

As a therapist who has worked with children and adolescents, the intensity can be lessened if fun can be had. However, always remind the child that fun is okay, and safety is the best friend of fun. We can have fun if you are safe, and so is everyone else. This is layered, but it is the step-by-step method that was previously mentioned. Once you convey the concept, begin to build on it to add other important ideas regarding emotional regulation.

What A Child Needs to Know About Their Emotions

The first thing that a child needs to know about their emotions is that they are not bad, stupid, make them an annoying person, make them weird, should make them feel scared, or any other negative conclusion they may have come to.

Children must know that emotions are a part of their human experience and their emotions are God given. The goal is to help them not only regulate their emotions but to understand them so that they can avoid shame or even embarrassment because of what they are feeling.

Here are a few simple phrases that can help children and adolescents feel seen, supported, and less alone in what they are experiencing.

  • “It’s okay to not feel okay.” – Normalizes odd feelings without judgement.
  • “Sadness can feel lonely. Can I sit with you quietly?” – Normalize maintaining connecting during tough times versus isolation.
  • “Crying is okay. I will get you some tissue.” – The focus is getting the child comfortable with being supported while being validated (seen).
  • “Feeling scared is hard. What do you need right now? – The focus is getting the child to speak to how to name what would meet their need, by using their words.

The key is to keep it simple, continue step-by-step and to model. Children need to see that we not only understand but are present. Being present is not just about our bodies being in the same space, meaning proximity. They need to know that an adult is present in their eyes and with their hearts. This matters to any child in any emotional state at any time.

Modeling is one of the most effective ways children learn emotional regulation. Children are always watching how the adults around them respond to frustration, sadness, disappointment, fear, and even joy.

When adults can slow down, name what is happening, and respond steadily, children begin to learn that emotions can be felt without taking over the whole moment. This is not about being perfect in front of a child. It is about allowing the child to see regulation practiced in real time.

One Step Further

The goal is to build a foundation of understanding not only emotional regulation but to also take it one step further to begin establishing good mental health. Think about that for a second, what if it was widespread practice to put into place the building blocks for children to have a good headstart to sound mental health.

Children who understand their emotions grow into adults who understand their emotions as well as how to manage them. Children can control their emotions when they learn that their emotions are a part of their human experience.

As a therapist who is a Christian, I can tell you that unpacking that truth, along with the reality that God equipped us with emotions for a purpose, and that they are good. God speaks of emotions and how to manage them throughout His Word.

A child must know that anger is real and God is aware. Fear is going to show up; God knew it and warned us that we were going to have to stand up to fear, not run from it. With God’s help, they can emotionally regulate.

Children are easy to teach when we know what we are teaching and how to teach it. When controlling emotions is taught with consideration of self, others, environment, and outcome, it helps to create step-by-step instruction, which creates consistency in demonstration and modeling.

As children grow into adolescents the emotional lessons that they learn will undoubtedly stick with them while allowing additional knowledge of more complicated emotional concepts.

Sensitivity can be learned, and due to our culture, which is heavily packed with less-kind television programming, video games, and movie entertainment, sensitivity is an emotion we cannot afford to leave children to gather on their own.

Teaching children how to manage anger and express it in a healthy way is a necessity our current society can no longer ignore. Ignoring emotional health until it becomes a crisis. When a child is in mental crisis, there is less chance of helping them, and it is harder to assist the appointed adult with comprehending what is happening with them in the moment.

The more clarity that can be given to children to help them identify and understand their emotions, the better we can help them manage what they go through while continuing to understand who they are and will become emotionally.

Photos:
“Girl Looking Out the Window”, Courtesy of bruce mars, Unsplash.com, CC0 License; “Carried by Mom”, Courtesy of Xavier Mouton Photographie, Unsplash.com, CC0 License

The post Is It Possible for Kids to Control their Emotions? A Child Therapist Weighs In appeared first on Bellevue Christian Counseling.

item.title: Is It Possible for Kids to Control their Emotions? A Child Therapist Weighs In

item.title: Attachment Issues: Signs, Causes, Effects, and Ways to Overcome
item.description:
Who are you as you relate to the people around you? If you pause long enough to consider the patterns of behavior that mark your interactions with other people, you might surprise yourself. The way you build relationships with others may be rooted in and display attachment issues. This can negatively affect those relationships. Identifying any attachment issues you may have and working on them can help you nurture healthier connections.

Healthy Relationships and Attachment Issues

If healthy relationships can be described as being rooted in trust, mutual dependence, openness, and security, attachment issues result in relationships that don’t have an abundance of these qualities. When a person has attachment issues, it means they struggle to depend on, trust, or feel secure with other people in their lives.

To dig a little deeper, attachment issues can be described as the patterns of difficulty a person experiences in being able to form or maintain emotional bonds with other people. These patterns are often rooted in formative early life experiences. Whether through early life or later experiences, the patterns set in motion shape how one relates to family, partners, friends, and even colleagues.

The concept of attachment issues comes from John Bowlby’s research in the mid-20th century about the way the quality of the bond formed between a primary caregiver and the child in their care helps to influence that child’s social, emotional, and relational development throughout their life. An insecure bond between the child and their caregiver can result in an insecure attachment style, leading to attachment issues.

Attachment issues can make it hard to have healthy and meaningful relationships with other people.

Signs and Patterns of Attachment Issues

When you have attachment issues, they can differ and vary in terms of their intensity as well as the range of behaviors they produce. Any attachment issues you may have may be displayed through various behaviors in daily life, such as the following:

Dependency or clinginess This may look like feeling anxious if a loved one isn’t constantly available. If they don’t read or immediately respond to messages, or if you don’t know where they are or who they’re with, that can make you feel anxious. You might also feel anxious about their love and constantly ask them to reassure you or make gestures that indicate they care about you.

Fear of intimacy or closeness Pushing people away when they get too close, or avoiding deep relationships altogether, is another pattern of attachment issues. When a relationship starts getting deep or requires commitment and intimacy, it can start to feel uncomfortable, and it’s easier to leave at that point, even if some part of you desires that closeness.

Difficulty trusting others Another attachment issue may look like expecting loved ones to betray you or abandon you, even without a clear reason for having such an expectation. When you expect betrayal or abandonment, it makes it hard to trust others because you could be hurt at any moment. This leads to not trusting or committing to others.

Emotional extremes A person with attachment issues might also experience emotional extremes such as intense affection followed by withdrawal. This push and pull is often the result of having a deep desire to connect but also carrying fears of betrayal and abandonment.

Overreacting to rejection or separation In relationships, conflict occurs, and it can create emotional and physical distance. For a person with attachment issues, this state of affairs can result in experiencing huge feelings of anxiety or anger.

People-pleasing and conflict avoidance One of the outcomes of attachment issues is being afraid of conflict and disagreements. You may worry that they signal the beginning of the end, or even the end of the relationship itself. As such, a person with attachment issues may find themselves seeking the approval of others at their own expense just to avoid conflict or disagreement.

The patterns of attachment issues can appear in small and subtle ways, such as those described above. They can show up as constantly checking for messages from a loved one, struggling to relax and just be in friendships, or feeling a sense of dread or panic if someone seems distant. It can also look like overdependence on others’ reassurance. In work settings, it could also look like a reluctance to collaborate closely with colleagues.

Some Causes of Attachment Issues, and Their Impact on Life and Relationships

Attachment issues will often stem from early relational experiences, but later life experiences can also result in attachment issues. In large measure, attachment issues are connected to an insecure attachment style that’s formed when a person’s needs for safety, comfort, and connection are violated, neglected, or met inconsistently. Some of the early life experiences that can result in attachment issues include:

Neglect or Abandonment This is when physical or emotional needs go repeatedly unmet. If a child doesn’t feel seen, if the adults around them don’t respond to bids for attention or for play, the child may develop the understanding that their needs don’t matter.

Inconsistent caregiving Just as damaging is when a caregiver is sometimes present and nurturing, but sometimes neglectful. Such inconsistent caregiving makes the child see life as unpredictable, and their needs as something that can’t reliably be met by others.

Loss or Major Life Disruptions Experiencing separation from caregivers, whether through frequent moves, divorce, or death, can result in attachment issues.

Trauma or Abuse When a child experiences fear or harm in their close relationships, that may also lead to developing attachment issues.

As influential as these early experiences are, later life experiences can also either reinforce or cultivate difficulties with attachment. These experiences include betrayals, long-term stress in relationships, or toxic relationships.

When you have attachment issues, it has a huge impact on how you experience trust, love, and friendships. Different attachment issues may show up in various struggles, such as feeling secure in your relationships. You might not quite feel at ease, able to simply enjoy the relationship and be loved.

Attachment issues can also make it hard to maintain healthy boundaries with other people. Instead of being able to place healthy limits on yourself for your well-being, you might easily violate them to please others. With attachment issues, it can be harder to communicate your needs without feeling guilt or fear. Lastly, attachment issues can result in experiencing prolonged loneliness or anxiety.

The different patterns of behavior that are associated with attachment issues can put you in situations where you experience isolation in your relationships, relationship conflict, or emotional exhaustion from violating your own boundaries.

How to Overcome Attachment Issues

Your past doesn’t dictate your future. Attachment issues aren’t a life sentence that you have no choice but to live with them. Old fears can be overcome, and you can learn as well as re-learn connection and trust. There are effective strategies that can help you heal from and overcome attachment issues.

Some strategies you can consider include the following:

Nurturing healthy self-awareness Knowing yourself can be a powerful tool that can help you set and maintain healthy boundaries, as well as understand your own reactions to situations. Through practices such as journaling or mindfulness, you’ll learn how to identify your own emotional triggers and responses. This will help you as you try to manage your emotions and how you relate to others you’re in a relationship with.

Learning emotional regulation Being able to handle your own emotions can take practical steps. Getting adequate sleep and managing other emotional triggers are helpful. It also includes practicing techniques to help manage anxiety, anger, and fear. These include mindfulness, breathing techniques, and visualization.

Re-parenting yourself This can include treating yourself with compassion and providing yourself with the comfort and reassurance you may have lacked as a child. You are fearfully and wonderfully made in the image of the Creator, and you matter (Genesis 1:26-28; Psalm 8, 139; Romans 5:8; 1 John 4:16-19). Embracing the reality of God’s love for you can make a remarkable difference in your life.

Building safe connections Taking the time to cultivate relationships with supportive and trustworthy people can help you reset your expectations and ability to relate to others in a healthy way.

Counseling and therapy Healing from attachment issues is a gradual process, and it’s one that takes intentionality. With help from a counselor or therapist, you can identify your patterns of attachment issues. Your counselor or therapist might use approaches such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to not only identify those unhealthy patterns, but also to reframe any false and damaging beliefs you may have about relationships.

If you need support to work through your attachment issues, be sure to browse our online counselor directory or contact our reception team. A counselor can help you begin your journey to overcome attachment issues and the concerns they raise in your relationships.

Photos:
“Woman in Denim”, Courtesy of Helena Lopes, Unsplash.com, CC0 License; “Shoes”, Courtesy of Eric Prouzet, Unsplash.com, CC0 License

The post Attachment Issues: Signs, Causes, Effects, and Ways to Overcome appeared first on Los Angeles Christian Counseling.

item.title: Curiosity or Dependency? Protecting Yourself From the Trap of AI Delusions and Developing Social Anxiety Disorder
item.description:
Artificial Intelligence is here and here to stay. Without us realizing it, it has already changed the way we live, work, and connect. This technology is now part of daily life, from chat tools to recommendation systems.

While these tools bring convenience, they also create new risks.

One of the fastest-growing concerns is the rise of what some experts have coined as AI delusions, which are false beliefs or distorted perceptions shaped by over-reliance on artificial intelligence. For people already struggling with mental health challenges like social anxiety disorder, this trend is posing an even greater risk and can make daily challenges even harder.

Let’s delve deeper into this and discuss how this AI curiosity can quickly turn into dependency as the first step toward protecting mental health.

Why AI Delusions are Growing so Quickly

AI delusions are not science fiction. They happen when people begin to trust artificial intelligence in ways that blur reality. For example, someone may start believing an AI tool understands their emotions better than friends or family, or they may rely on it for constant reassurance.

These beliefs are growing rapidly because AI systems are designed to respond quickly, mimic human conversation, and provide personalized feedback.

The growth of AI delusions is tied to how accessible these tools have become. They are available on phones, laptops, and even smart home devices. The more people interact with them, the easier it is to slip into thinking they provide more than they really do. Curiosity about new technology is natural, but when curiosity turns into dependency, the risks increase. Overreliance upon AI and isolation leads to living outside of how God has created you, in His image. Fellowship with others, prayer, and community are essentials to a full life, and something that a dependence upon AI cannot satisfy.

Where the Line Gets Blurry

Curiosity is healthy. Trying out new tools, learning how they work, and exploring their benefits is part of adapting to modern life. Dependency, however, is different.

It happens whenever someone begins to rely on anything for emotional support, decision-making, or validation. With AI, the line between curiosity and dependency blurs when the bot starts eliminating actual human connection to unhealthy levels.

For example, checking in with an AI tool for advice once in a while is curiosity. Turning to it every hour of the day for reassurance about personal worth or social interactions can quickly cross the line into dependency. This dependency can quietly grow until it feels normal, making it harder to recognize when habits have become unhealthy.

Not everyone is equally vulnerable to AI delusions. Certain people are more likely to lean on these tools in ways that blur reality.

Who is Most Likely to Fall into the AI Dependency Trap

  • People who already struggle with loneliness or limited social support are at higher risk. When human connection feels difficult or unavailable, AI can seem like a safe substitute.
  • Younger users who grew up with technology also face unique risks. They are comfortable with digital interaction, which makes it easier to slip into believing AI provides genuine companionship.
  • Another group at risk includes individuals under constant pressure, like students, office professionals, or caregivers, who are likely to turn to AI for quick answers and reassurance. Over time, this reliance grows into dependency, especially if they believe the tool understands them better than people around them.
  • Those living with social anxiety disorder are especially vulnerable because interacting with AI feels less stressful than facing real conversations.

The common thread is not weakness, but circumstance. When stress, isolation, or anxiety are present, AI feels like an easy solution. Recognizing these patterns helps explain why the trend is growing so quickly and why awareness is essential. Understanding who is most at risk makes it easier to take steps that protect mental health before dependency deepens.

Common Misconceptions About AI and Mental Health

One misconception is that AI can replace therapy or counseling. While AI tools may provide information or coping tips, they are not trained professionals. Another misconception is that AI understands emotions in the same way humans do. In reality, AI responds based on patterns and data, not genuine empathy.

A third misconception is that using AI for social support is harmless. For someone with social anxiety disorder, relying on AI instead of practicing real-world interactions can reinforce isolation. These misconceptions feed into the growth of AI delusions, making it important to separate fact from fiction.

How AI Delusions Feed into Social Anxiety Disorder

Social anxiety disorder involves fear of judgment, rejection, or embarrassment in social situations. AI delusions can make this worse. When someone believes AI offers safer or more reliable interaction than people, they may withdraw from real relationships. This withdrawal reinforces anxiety, creating a cycle that is hard to break.

AI delusions also feed into distorted thinking. For example, if an AI tool provides constant positive feedback, the person may begin to believe that only AI understands them, increasing anxiety in real social settings, where feedback is more complex and less predictable. Over time, the reliance on AI deepens the disorder instead of helping it.

Examples and Signs Your Relationship with AI Might Be Risky

There are clear signs that curiosity has turned into dependency. These include:

  • Spending more time talking to AI tools than to friends or family
  • Feeling anxious or unsettled when not using AI for reassurance
  • Believing AI understands personal struggles better than people do
  • Avoiding social situations because AI feels safer
  • Relying on AI for decisions that should involve personal judgment or human advice

These signs show that the relationship with AI is no longer balanced. Recognizing them early helps prevent deeper issues.

Simple daily habits help maintain balance.

Daily Habits to Help Keep You Grounded in Reality

  • Limiting time spent with AI tools is one step. Setting aside time for face-to-face conversations, even short ones, reinforces real connection.
  • Writing down personal thoughts in a journal instead of relying on AI for feedback encourages self-reflection.
  • Seeking information from trusted human sources instead of relying solely on AI ensures balanced perspectives.
  • Another helpful habit is practicing mindfulness. Paying attention to real surroundings, sounds, and interactions keeps the mind grounded in reality.
  • Prayer, community, and other methods of expanding social connectedness to assist in being present.
  • Choosing activities that involve creativity, exercise, or nature also reduces dependency on technology.
  • It is also helpful to diversify online activities. Instead of using AI for everything, mix in educational videos, podcasts, or online communities that involve real people.

Such simple, traditional habits we used to take for advantage are the key to helping us remember that fulfillment comes from real experiences, not digital illusions.

Protecting mental health online starts with awareness. Questioning how much time is spent with AI tools and why they are being used is important. Setting boundaries, such as designated offline hours, helps reduce dependency.

This variety reduces the risk of falling into AI delusions and supports healthier online habits.

Seeking Support When AI Disillusionment Turns into Anxiety

When disillusionment with AI or dependency begins to affect your daily life, professional support might be what you need to help steer you right again.

Counselors and life coaches are there to provide guidance in a personal way that AI cannot. They help identify unhealthy patterns, build coping strategies, and encourage real-world connections. For those with social anxiety disorder, professional support is especially important. It provides a safe space to explore fears and develop healthier ways of relating to others.

AI delusions are growing quickly because technology is designed to feel personal and responsive. While curiosity about these tools is natural, dependency creates risks, especially for those living with social anxiety disorder. Recognizing misconceptions, spotting warning signs, and building daily habits that keep life grounded are key steps toward protecting mental health.

If you have realized that your relationship with AI has already become too dependent and your online habits are affecting your well-being, professional help is an important step forward. Counselors and life coaches are available on this site to guide you through these challenges and help you find peace and purpose again.

Contact our office today to speak with our reception team and schedule an appointment with me or another qualified Christian Counselor in our network. You can learn to have a healthier future.

Photos:
“On the Phone”, Courtesy of Jonas Leupe, Unsplash.com, CC0 License

The post Curiosity or Dependency? Protecting Yourself From the Trap of AI Delusions and Developing Social Anxiety Disorder appeared first on Spokane Christian Counseling.

item.title: Beauty from Ashes: God’s Healing Work Through Heartbreak and Loss
item.description:
To all who mourn in Israel, he will give a crown of beauty for ashes, a joyous blessing instead of mourning, festive praise instead of despair. In their righteousness, they will be like great oaks that the LORD has planted for his own glory. –  Isaiah 61:3, NLT

Everyone experiences disappointment. At some point in life, we all encounter heartbreak, loss, betrayal, rejection, or circumstances that leave us wondering how we will ever move forward. We live in a fallen world, and the world has a way of letting us down. People fail us. Dreams don’t unfold as planned. Doors close unexpectedly. Life doesn’t always deliver what we hoped for.

Giving Heartbreak to God

What do we do with those feelings? How do we respond when life seems to fall apart?

…we know that God causes everything to work together for the good of those who love God and are called according to his purpose for them. – Romans 8:28, NLT

Notice that Scripture says everything – not just the victories, blessings, and successes. God works through the failures, disappointments, losses, and painful seasons as well. The very things that seem to derail us often become the path through which God accomplishes His purposes.

Over the years, both my husband and I have experienced firsthand what it means for God to bring beauty from ashes. Though our stories are different, they share a common theme: what felt like devastation became the place where God was at work, redeeming what once seemed lost. Looking back, we can both see Romans 8:28 and Isaiah 61:3 woven throughout our journeys.

Ten years ago, a significant event occurred that changed the course of both my life and my marriage. I found myself in a deep, dark place. It felt as though my world was crashing down around me. I thought the life I knew was over.

Yet even in that darkness, I sensed God’s presence. Though I couldn’t see how things would work out, I held on to the promise that He would somehow redeem what felt broken. I clung to the hope found in Isaiah 61:3 – that God could bring beauty from ashes, joy from mourning, and praise from despair. One year later, God gave me a visual. I kept seeing flowers, plants, or other vegetation blooming through volcanic ash or solidified lava.

Think about a volcanic eruption. At the moment, it leaves nothing but devastation. Everything in its path is buried, burned, or destroyed. It appears hopeless. Yet God designed creation so that even volcanic destruction can become the foundation for new life. The ash and minerals enrich the soil. Over time, new growth emerges. Entire ecosystems are reborn, sometimes more vibrant than before.

As the anniversary of that painful season approached, I found myself reflecting on how far God had brought me. While traces of old grief occasionally surfaced, I could clearly see His faithfulness. Just like those small plants pushing through the ash, God had been restoring me and our marriage – piece by piece.

Around that same time, several worship songs seemed to echo the message God was teaching me. One song reminded me that we were “made to rise” above difficult circumstances. Another spoke of how God often uses people with scars rather than those who appear perfect. Yet another declared, “I see shattered, You see whole. I see broken, but You see beautiful.”

Those lyrics resonated deeply because they reflected what God had been doing in my life. What looked ruined wasn’t beyond His reach. What felt lost wasn’t wasted.

That season was marked by betrayal, loss, and the challenging work of rebuilding. Yet looking back, I can see Romans 8:28 in action. God did not waste the pain. He used it and made things better than they were before.

The Bible and Heartbreak

Many people struggle with disappointment because they expect life, relationships, careers, or circumstances to fulfill something only God can provide. The world continually promises satisfaction yet repeatedly falls short.

From a counseling perspective, disappointment often carries secondary emotions that people don’t immediately recognize. Beneath the sadness may be grief. Beneath the anger may be hurt. Beneath the fear may be a sense of lost identity or unmet expectations. Many people become stuck because they try to push those feelings down or away rather than acknowledge them.

Healing rarely happens by pretending we are unaffected by our circumstances. Healing begins when we honestly bring our pain before God, allow ourselves to process what has been lost, and trust Him to work it out for good.

Scripture is filled with examples of people who grieved, lamented, questioned, and struggled. Yet their stories remind us that pain and faith can coexist. We do not have to choose between trusting God and being honest about our disappointment.

The Bible also powerfully illustrates how God redeems human adversity and hardships by consistently transforming trials, tribulations, pain, and adversity into ultimate good for those who love Him. This fundamental promise provides believers with the assurance that every aspect of their story has a purpose under God’s divine guidance. Perhaps that disappointment serves a greater purpose than we realize.

If you are navigating a difficult season and finding it hard to see beyond the pain, Christian counseling may be a helpful resource. A trained Christian counselor can help you process emotions, identify unhealthy patterns, strengthen coping skills, and explore how biblical truth applies to your unique circumstances. While counseling cannot remove the hardship, it can provide support, encouragement, and practical tools as you move toward healing and restoration.

Romans 8

Recently, my husband shared a similar message with the young adults at our church. As I read his notes, I realized how closely they connected with what God had taught both of us through our own difficult seasons.

He reminded them, “The world disappoints – it lets you down. But Romans 8:28 reframes every letdown as something God is actively working through for your good.” He called it “The Beautiful Letdown.” He explained that the “letdown” becomes the vehicle of God’s purpose. When we look closely at Romans 8:28, we see several powerful truths:

“All things” – This is not just the victories, but the failures, rejections, and disappointments. The moments where the world didn’t deliver. Those moments – the letdowns – are actually where something real is happening.

“Work for the good” – The letdown isn’t wasted. God takes the very thing that hurt or disappointed you and uses it redemptively.

  • The dissatisfaction we feel with this world is not necessarily a spiritual problem – it can be a gift. It keeps us from settling for temporary things and reminds us that we were created for something more.
  • When you’re dissatisfied with the world, it keeps you focused on more important things.
  • This place isn’t our home…we’re just passing through en route to a better place.

“Called according to his purpose” – this is why the letdown is beautiful. You were called to something beyond what this world offers. The disappointment is confirmation that you belong somewhere else.

The world will always let you down, and that’s exactly what God uses to keep your eyes on Him. There is only One who will never let you down or disappoint you: God.

Revelation 21:4 NLT tells us, “He will wipe every tear from their eyes, and there will be no more death or sorrow or crying or pain. All these things are gone forever.”

  • The beautiful letdown is Romans 8:28 in experience.
  • What felt like loss was actually God working.
  • What felt like rejection was redirection.
  • What felt like the world closing a door was God reminding you that this was never your home to begin with.

Looking back now, we can clearly see God’s hand at work in what once felt like complete devastation. For my husband, exactly one year after his painful season, he met me – the woman who would become his wife. Today, we have been married for thirty-one years.

Years later, during one of the most painful seasons of our marriage, I experienced my own “beauty from ashes” story. Instead of walking away, we made the decision to fight for our marriage rather than fight with each other.

In both of our stories, what once felt like ashes became something beautiful. What felt like an ending became a new beginning. And through it all, God proved Himself faithful. What once looked like ashes became a testimony of His grace, reminding us that He truly does give beauty for ashes.

“Lava Field”, Courtesy of Alexander Shenkin, Unsplash.com, CC0 License; 

The post Beauty from Ashes: God’s Healing Work Through Heartbreak and Loss appeared first on Tacoma Christian Counseling.

item.title: Choosing Positive Reactions to Manage Stress
item.description:
It’s no secret that life is full of surprises. With technology, bad news travels quickly. Bad news can trigger stress for many people. Stress, in turn, triggers health problems. The general population in America today is becoming more stress-aware. More people are deciding to get healthy and learn to manage stress. By choosing to manage stress, individuals can enhance their quality of life. Stress management tips often include understanding positive reactions.

As Christians, our lifestyle should reflect peace rather than chaos. Chaos can be consuming and destructive not only for ourselves but also for those around us. This is not the life God intends for us. Stress management is a choice that an individual must make to maintain a healthy lifestyle. Worrying does not change anything about circumstances or the outcome; it only changes the way our body and mind feel.

Scripture is clear about the fruitlessness of worry:

And which of you by worrying can add a day to his life’s span? – Luke 12:25, NASB

Knowing the Symptoms of Stress

It’s normal to experience stressful situations in life. Stress can be found on the job, at home, raising kids, going to the grocery store, and even driving in traffic. No one is completely free from experiencing stressful situations. The key thing to remember is that managing stress decreases its effects.

Stress affects a person’s body and mind, which can result in disturbances at work, school, or even at home. To react to stress positively, it’s important to identify the symptoms that come with stress. Here is a short list of the most common symptoms of stress:

  • Constant fatigue
  • Insomnia
  • Digestion issues
  • Headaches
  • Anxiety or panic attacks
  • Mood swings
  • Weight changes
  • Inability to concentrate
  • Fatigue
  • Body tension

All of these symptoms may not be present when experiencing stress, but most of the time, people experience at least five. Whether you experience two symptoms or six, it is still important to understand how to react positively to stress.

Tips for Stress Management

Reacting positively can be done in a multitude of ways. Understanding how to react positively when dealing with stress can decrease the amount of time you spend worrying. Some of the ways to react positively revolve around thought patterns, and others revolve around activities. The following stress management tips can help reduce the effects of stress on the body and mind.

Maintain a dedicated quiet time and read Scripture

Having a dedicated time of day for Bible reading can greatly increase how an individual faces stressful situations. This can also help create mindful quotes that can be recalled when a person is feeling overwhelmed in certain circumstances.

Exercise for fun

Keeping physical activity at the forefront of a daily routine will also help reduce the negative impact of stress. Engaging in exercise in a fun way promotes a more joyful outlook on the situation you may encounter. One of the best ways to make it fun is to include a friend.

Write down the good stuff

Keeping a journal doesn’t have to be mundane and boring. Grab some markers, colors, and fun stickers, and take time to write down the good stuff. Journal about the moments of gratitude you have experienced, and keep track of the inspirational things you’ve seen in a day. These types of things can relieve stress and bring out the best part of the day.

Delight in the pleasures of life

Just as life has stresses, it also has pleasures. Pleasure can come in a variety of ways depending on the person. Take time to enjoy your favorite hobbies or experiences regularly. For instance, camping, sitting around a fire pit, or simply curling up with a good book are pleasures in life that are considered positive reactions to stress.

Set boundaries and reduce negative people

When it comes to positive reactions to stress, it is important to maintain boundaries to reduce negative people or a toxic mindset. Keeping positive people in your life will encourage you to maintain positive reactions while you try to manage stress. This also includes encouraging yourself and having positive self-talk.

Remember it’s okay to laugh

Even though you may be facing a stressful situation, always remember that it’s OK to find humor in the things that happen every day. Learning to find laughter in the middle of stress is one of the best ways to relieve stress, reduce its effects, and find the positive aspects of the situation.

Take on a self-challenge

Sometimes setting a goal or challenge can help with stress management. Trying a new sport can become a way of refocusing your thoughts. An exercise challenge can not only help you refocus, but it will also promote a healthier lifestyle. Consider all kinds of things that could be challenges, then choose ones that appeal to your interests. You could have a reading challenge, a gardening challenge, or even a coffee challenge. The key is to choose something fun and challenge yourself.

Volunteer to help others

Helping others through volunteer work has been proven to reduce stress. By helping others, you create a mindset that encourages positivity. You could also choose a way to brighten someone’s day with a simple gesture of friendship. For instance, picking up an extra cup of coffee in the morning as you head to the office. Doing things for others helps you feel better.

Keep track of the positive things

As you journal each night, you may want to dedicate one page to the positive things of the day. Listing three positive things each day can encourage you to become mindful during the day to look for the positive, even in the middle of a stressful situation.

You can’t change things

One of the most important stress management tips is to realize you can’t always change the situation. There are times when things happen, and we cannot control them. Those are the times we have to realize we do what we can and let the rest go.

Rest is best

The way stress can affect the body can cause a person to lose sleep. To overcome this problem, it’s helpful to have some form of relaxation that will promote a restful night. Cell phones and TV are some of the major contributors to lack of sleep. The suggestion is to turn off the devices and the TV and read a magazine or book to help calm your mind.

Organization brings peace

Wherever your workspace is, it is important to have an organized space. Being able to locate the tools or resources you need to complete a job will reduce the chance of being stressed because of clutter. A home that is clean and organized can also reduce feelings of chaos, not just for you but for the entire family.

Therapy helps

In cases of extreme anxiety, it is beneficial to work with a Christian counselor. This can help identify triggers, understand symptoms, implement techniques, and create a faith-based plan that promotes a positive mindset. It’s OK to realize that sometimes you can’t do it on your own. Getting help from a Christian counselor improves your stress response.

Help for Managing Stress

Learning how to use stress management tips to reduce stress is one of the best ways to react positively to a stressful situation. Remember that a healthy lifestyle, a positive thought process, and understanding your reactions can lead to a lower stress level and better health.

If you or a loved one is struggling with overwhelming stress, reach out to your local Christian counselor. They can help you navigate stress management tips that will work for you. If you’re not sure where to start, the staff in the office can help. Call today to learn how a Christian counselor can help you better manage your stress.

The post Choosing Positive Reactions to Manage Stress appeared first on Spokane Christian Counseling.

item.title: What is Healthy and Unhealthy Stress?
item.description:
What is stress, and how does it occur? Is stress only ever harmful? How does one’s faith impact stress? This article will focus on the biological, psychological, social, and spiritual components of stress. Awareness of stress is imperative, especially in a time when society feels more stressful than ever.

Biological Stress

The brain has a direct involvement in how stress is experienced and how it becomes more intense in certain situations than others. Cortisol, a stress hormone, is the primary influence in a stressful situation. The release of cortisol from the brain indicates that our attention and body need to become focused on a specific thing, event, or person(s).

In addition to cortisol, other hormones such as adrenaline and endorphins are also simultaneously released if the stressful event/situation suggests we may be in physical danger. This process comes from several parts of the brain, including the thalamus (brain relay station), the hypothalamus (primary function is to maintain balance), the amygdala (the emotional regulator), and the autonomic nervous system (state of activation and relaxation).

All these parts of the brain are used to initiate, control, and influence our fight-or-flight response to stressful situations. This can be seen in situations where there is a genuine physical threat (i.e., someone directly confronting you in public) or loud noises around you, but you have no direct interaction with them. In addition, too much cortisol in the body can cause difficulty losing weight and/or cause weight gain.

Ever notice when you are stressed and all you feel like having is some type of comfort food? That is because the chronic or long-term release of cortisol impacts your appetite regulation system (i.e., “…excess cortisol stimulates hunger-inducing hormones like ghrelin and reduces the brain’s sensitivity to satiety signals like leptin”) (Spencer, S.J. 2019).

Situational or Psychological Stress

Are certain amounts of stress normal, or is all stress bad? According to the World Health Organization (WHO), stress can be a good thing if it is used effectively. For example, say you’re a student in school, and you’re preparing for an exam. A certain amount of stress can be used as a motivator to maintain concentration and do well on the exam.

However, if you do not study enough and know you are not well prepared for the exam, you will stress even more and have a higher chance of losing any retained information (i.e., test anxiety). Most people nonchalantly say “I have anxiety” but don’t always recognize the significance of such a simple statement.

While there is a normal level of stress or nervousness for new things, transitions, or unexpected changes, anxiety has a more profound impact on people’s lives. Anxiety disorders are caused when the stress is so overwhelming that it cannot be controlled. In addition, anxiety typically impacts the person’s life in more ways than one.

According to the American Psychiatric Association (APA), the U.S. general population is diagnosed with roughly 19% (APA, 2022). This translates to about 19% of the population in the United States living with overwhelming amounts of stress that prevent them from doing their jobs, going to school, managing money, or even having interpersonal/intimate relationships.

Now let’s look even further into the negative impacts stress can have on oneself if not properly monitored and/or managed. Overwhelming amounts of stress can have both cognitive and behavioral impacts on a person. For example, when we are too stressed, we tend to forget things more, have difficulty retaining new information, or have difficulty recalling information.

As one could imagine, this would not only cause more stress but could also create other issues such as poor eating habits, depression, isolation, and even panic attacks. In addition, too much stress can affect your ability to control your impulses and avoid overreacting. Have you ever noticed you were having a rough day, maybe at work, at school, or even something with your kids, and you just feel overwhelmed?

Now imagine some small inconvenience – nothing you would normally afford much attention to sets you off! Maybe that frustration gets taken out on a spouse, a kid, a pet, a friend, a family member, etc. Learning to balance your stress in your daily life can help prevent these negative aspects of stress.

Spiritual Impacts from Stress

How is stress impacting your spiritual walk in your faith? Do you feel like you are closer to God when you are more stressed? Some people feel they are closer because they will naturally lean more toward God in order to find comfort during uncertain times. However, how does stress impact your ability to distinguish between God’s voice and the voice of the enemy?

The Bible says in John 10:10, “The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy; I have come that they may have life and have it to the full.” The enemy does not come into your life in full force when you are doing well. He comes into your life when you are low and begin to have doubts.

Have you ever noticed that people will often say, “Well, if God is almighty and all-powerful, then why does (fill in the blank) happen?” The enemy wants you to not put your faith in God or believe that you need God. The enemy will try to lead you in ways that not only keep you focused on him and not on God but maintain an elevated level of stress, which will naturally exhaust you even further.

What are some ways stress may be impacting your spirituality? How often do you read the Bible? Or when you do read the Bible, what are you getting from it? Do the words resonate with you, or are they just words? Do you pray, and are your prayers meaningful? I’m not talking about praying over dinner; I mean really praying with conviction and belief that God hears your prayers and will answer them.

Do you listen to worship music regularly? Not just listening to the cool Forrest Frank songs, but really letting your body, mind, and soul connect with the words and even at times cause an emotional reaction (i.e., crying). When you are too stressed, you do fewer of the good spiritual things that strengthen your faith and give in to worldly temptations, which only cause even more, you guessed it – stress!

How do you remedy excessive stress?

There are several effective methods for mitigating excessive stress. First, take an honest assessment of yourself and see if you are feeling joy in your day-to-day life. Do you feel present most days at work, school, home, social events, etc.? Do they seem to connect genuinely with the relationships you have, or do they seem only surface-level? Do you just feel like you are on autopilot and almost seem numb to more stress being added to your pile?

After taking that honest assessment, what do you think you are doing right, and what do you think you are doing wrong? Ask people you trust to provide constructive criticism on how they see you handling stressful situations. Sometimes, we think we know what we are doing and that we know ourselves better, so we become guarded to external opinions.

However, if you only rely on your self-assessment, you leave room for error. Finally, make necessary adjustments to better reduce stress and improve your overall quality of life. Although the world seems to be in a stressful state most of the time these days, it is possible to find balance. Take things one step at a time and celebrate each of your daily accomplishments.

For example, you can go for a walk with no distractions, stay more hydrated and eat better, get more sleep, live with fewer distractions (e.g., screen time, social media, etc.), or even avoid being around groups of people that do not add value to your life but who detract from your overall sense of peace and balance.

When you feel like you are becoming too stressed, in the moment, take some deep breaths, close your eyes, and just imagine being in a place that brings you peace. These are effective methods of reducing harmful stress and allowing yourself to process good stress in a productive way.

References:
American Psychiatric Association. (2022). “Diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders (5th ed., text rev.).” https://doi.org/10.1176/appi.books.9780890425787
Spencer, S.J. (2019). “How stress can (sometimes) make us eat more.” From Young Minds 7:95. doi: 10.3389/frym.2019.00095
World Health Organization (2026), “What is stress?” Retrieved from: https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/stress

Photo:
“Stressed Out”, Andrej Lišakov, Unsplash.com, Unsplash+ License

The post What is Healthy and Unhealthy Stress? appeared first on Tacoma Christian Counseling.

item.title: Bible Verses for Overeating Disorder
item.description:
Is overeating a struggle for you? Many of us face this struggle daily in our abundant culture, where food is tempting and readily available. However, the Bible can help you have better health by reminding you to curb your overeating habits.

When you use specific verses of God’s Word to prepare yourself, you can fight back with confidence when you are tempted to overeat. Jesus used Scripture to fight temptation at a time when he was very hungry (Matt. 4:1-11). If he did this to overcome Satan, we can do the same thing to gain spiritual victory.

The following verses are powerful weapons for you to fight temptation. Meditate on them, memorize them, write them down, post them where you see them often, and save them to your phone. The more ways you hide God’s Word in your heart, the more easily you will remember it when you are tempted to overeat. You can ask the Holy Spirit to bring them to mind when you need accountability in your eating habits.

The Best Bible Verses for Overeating Disorder

You can turn each of the following verses into a prayer in times of temptation. God will meet you right in those moments and give you the strength to overcome. He promises to deliver you from whatever temptation you face, and he will empower you to make better choices for your health.

…the rules of the Lord are true, and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, even much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and drippings of the honeycomb. – Psalm 19:9b-10

God considers his laws to be more desirable than the sweetest food available during Bible times – honey. His laws are more desirable than the finest gold, or perhaps your food craving of choice: chips, French fries, doughnuts, ice cream, pizza, or whatever tempts you most.

Remember that when you follow God’s laws, you will be blessed with a clean conscience. You won’t be riddled with guilt and shame like you may be when you overeat. God will help you make wise eating choices so you can live a disciplined life for his Kingdom work. His laws lead to life, while our poor choices lead to destruction, so remember this verse when you are tempted.

So I will bless you as long as I live; in your name I will lift up my hands. My soul will be satisfied as with fat and rich food, and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips. – Psalm 63:4-5

What are the richest foods you have tasted? Steak, lobster, cheesecake, or something else? Are you honestly as satisfied with God as you are when you eat these rich foods? You can learn to be more satisfied with God’s presence than you are with food, though this will take discipline.

The peace you find in God’s presence lasts much longer than the pleasure you get from eating rich food. When you learn to gain your true satisfaction from God, your faith will be grounded even while food looks tempting to you.

Delight yourself in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart. – Psalm 37:4

What are the desires of your heart when you are tempted to overeat? It’s probably not to simply feel full or enjoy the taste and texture of food. Most of us overeat to soothe our emotions and fill a place inside that feels empty. Often people with overeating disorders deal with loneliness, rejection, anxiety, depression, and other problems.

A caring Christian counselor can help you get to the roots of why you overeat. You can learn that taking delight in the Lord is much more satisfying than overeating, and you can trust him with the deepest desires of your heart.

How sweet are your words to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth! – Psalm 119:103

God’s Word will become sweeter to you the more you meditate on it, study it, and apply it to your life. The Bible has healing properties, just like real honey does. But God’s Word heals you with God’s love, comfort, encouragement, protection, and joy as you learn to relax in his presence and enjoy time with him. Each day, meet with God for a few minutes, asking him to make his words sweeter than honey to you and healing for your soul.

Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth; keep watch over the door of my lips! Do not let my heart incline to any evil, to busy myself with wicked deeds in company with men who work iniquity, and let me not eat of their delicacies! – Psalm 141:3-4

These verses address the issue of controlling what we say. But they can also apply to what food passes over our lips. We can ask God to stand guard over our lips when we are faced with a tempting situation.

He will help you stop putting things into your mouth that aren’t good for you. You can ask God to keep you from drifting toward evil choices and help you avoid the wrong kinds of delicacies. The next time you are tempted, simply pray “Guard my lips,” and God will be right beside you.

I cry to you, O Lord; I say, “You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living.” – Psalm 142:5

When you feel like you want that third piece of cake or fourth slice of pizza, you can pray this verse. You can say, “Lord, I think I want this food right now. But I know my true craving should be for you because you alone can satisfy me.” Then walk away from the temptation, drink a glass of water, and engage in a different activity. God will be your refuge in that moment, a haven where you can find comfort that lasts longer than the food you are craving.

If you have found honey, eat only enough for you, lest you have your fill of it and vomit it. – Proverbs 25:16

The Bible is eminently practical. Any food, even healthy food like honey, can make you sick if you overeat. Choose to eat a balanced diet of nourishing foods to protect your health and feel your best. When you are tempted to overeat in certain food categories, remember this verse and don’t succumb to temptation.

Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” – Matthew 26:41

Our minds and spirits may be willing to make wise food choices, but the sinful nature of our flesh is vulnerable to temptation. All of us face this scenario at one time or another, particularly when we are stressed. But God will help you in the very moment of temptation if you cry out to him. Admit to him that your flesh is weak, and ask him to deliver you from the temptation to overeat.

No temptation has overtaken you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your ability, but with the temptation, he will also provide the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it. – 1 Corinthians 10:13

This verse can be a practical comfort to you in times of temptation. Ask God to provide you a way out when you are about to overeat. He might instruct you to remove tempting foods from your pantry or eat a mini-meal before going to a restaurant. You can form more practical strategies to serve as escape routes with a qualified Christian counselor.

Christian Counseling for Overeating

The roots of overeating run deep for most people. You may need help from a Christian counselor to overcome overeating disorder. A counselor will offer Bible-based care with compassion and understanding. Your counselor will encourage you with principles that can keep you on track for a healthier lifestyle.

Photo:
“Plate with Cake”, Courtesy of Olivie Strauss, Unsplash.com, CC0 License

The post Bible Verses for Overeating Disorder appeared first on Mill Creek Christian Counseling.

item.title: Bible Verses for Overeating Disorder
item.description:
Is overeating a struggle for you? Many of us face this struggle daily in our abundant culture, where food is tempting and readily available. However, the Bible can help you have better health by reminding you to curb your overeating habits.

When you use specific verses of God’s Word to prepare yourself, you can fight back with confidence when you are tempted to overeat. Jesus used Scripture to fight temptation at a time when he was very hungry (Matt. 4:1-11). If he did this to overcome Satan, we can do the same thing to gain spiritual victory.

The following verses are powerful weapons for you to fight temptation. Meditate on them, memorize them, write them down, post them where you see them often, and save them to your phone. The more ways you hide God’s Word in your heart, the more easily you will remember it when you are tempted to overeat. You can ask the Holy Spirit to bring them to mind when you need accountability in your eating habits.

The Best Bible Verses for Overeating Disorder

You can turn each of the following verses into a prayer in times of temptation. God will meet you right in those moments and give you the strength to overcome. He promises to deliver you from whatever temptation you face, and he will empower you to make better choices for your health.

…the rules of the Lord are true, and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, even much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and drippings of the honeycomb. – Psalm 19:9b-10

God considers his laws to be more desirable than the sweetest food available during Bible times – honey. His laws are more desirable than the finest gold, or perhaps your food craving of choice: chips, French fries, doughnuts, ice cream, pizza, or whatever tempts you most.

Remember that when you follow God’s laws, you will be blessed with a clean conscience. You won’t be riddled with guilt and shame like you may be when you overeat. God will help you make wise eating choices so you can live a disciplined life for his Kingdom work. His laws lead to life, while our poor choices lead to destruction, so remember this verse when you are tempted.

So I will bless you as long as I live; in your name I will lift up my hands. My soul will be satisfied as with fat and rich food, and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips. – Psalm 63:4-5

What are the richest foods you have tasted? Steak, lobster, cheesecake, or something else? Are you honestly as satisfied with God as you are when you eat these rich foods? You can learn to be more satisfied with God’s presence than you are with food, though this will take discipline.

The peace you find in God’s presence lasts much longer than the pleasure you get from eating rich food. When you learn to gain your true satisfaction from God, your faith will be grounded even while food looks tempting to you.

Delight yourself in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart. – Psalm 37:4

What are the desires of your heart when you are tempted to overeat? It’s probably not to simply feel full or enjoy the taste and texture of food. Most of us overeat to soothe our emotions and fill a place inside that feels empty. Often people with overeating disorders deal with loneliness, rejection, anxiety, depression, and other problems.

A caring Christian counselor can help you get to the roots of why you overeat. You can learn that taking delight in the Lord is much more satisfying than overeating, and you can trust him with the deepest desires of your heart.

How sweet are your words to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth! – Psalm 119:103

God’s Word will become sweeter to you the more you meditate on it, study it, and apply it to your life. The Bible has healing properties, just like real honey does. But God’s Word heals you with God’s love, comfort, encouragement, protection, and joy as you learn to relax in his presence and enjoy time with him. Each day, meet with God for a few minutes, asking him to make his words sweeter than honey to you and healing for your soul.

Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth; keep watch over the door of my lips! Do not let my heart incline to any evil, to busy myself with wicked deeds in company with men who work iniquity, and let me not eat of their delicacies! – Psalm 141:3-4

These verses address the issue of controlling what we say. But they can also apply to what food passes over our lips. We can ask God to stand guard over our lips when we are faced with a tempting situation.

He will help you stop putting things into your mouth that aren’t good for you. You can ask God to keep you from drifting toward evil choices and help you avoid the wrong kinds of delicacies. The next time you are tempted, simply pray “Guard my lips,” and God will be right beside you.

I cry to you, O Lord; I say, “You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living.” – Psalm 142:5

When you feel like you want that third piece of cake or fourth slice of pizza, you can pray this verse. You can say, “Lord, I think I want this food right now. But I know my true craving should be for you because you alone can satisfy me.” Then walk away from the temptation, drink a glass of water, and engage in a different activity. God will be your refuge in that moment, a haven where you can find comfort that lasts longer than the food you are craving.

If you have found honey, eat only enough for you, lest you have your fill of it and vomit it. – Proverbs 25:16

The Bible is eminently practical. Any food, even healthy food like honey, can make you sick if you overeat. Choose to eat a balanced diet of nourishing foods to protect your health and feel your best. When you are tempted to overeat in certain food categories, remember this verse and don’t succumb to temptation.

Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” – Matthew 26:41

Our minds and spirits may be willing to make wise food choices, but the sinful nature of our flesh is vulnerable to temptation. All of us face this scenario at one time or another, particularly when we are stressed. But God will help you in the very moment of temptation if you cry out to him. Admit to him that your flesh is weak, and ask him to deliver you from the temptation to overeat.

No temptation has overtaken you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your ability, but with the temptation, he will also provide the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it. – 1 Corinthians 10:13

This verse can be a practical comfort to you in times of temptation. Ask God to provide you a way out when you are about to overeat. He might instruct you to remove tempting foods from your pantry or eat a mini-meal before going to a restaurant. You can form more practical strategies to serve as escape routes with a qualified Christian counselor.

Christian Counseling for Overeating

The roots of overeating run deep for most people. You may need help from a Christian counselor to overcome overeating disorder. A counselor will offer Bible-based care with compassion and understanding. Your counselor will encourage you with principles that can keep you on track for a healthier lifestyle.
